text: National University of Computer & Emerging Sciences - NUCES - Karachi Department of Artificial Intelligence The Power of Composition Because translation, rotation, and scaling are now aLL formatted uniformly as 3 x 3 matrix multiplications, they speak the exact same mathematical language. A computer can multiply a scale matrix, a rotation matrix, and a translation matrix together into one single "master matrix" before touching the geometry. The graphics engine then only has to perform one single matrix multiplication per pixel to apply all three transformations simultaneously. 6.2 Projective Transformations Projective transformations, or homographies, are a broader category of geometric mapping that break the strict rules of affine transformations to simulate how human eyes and cameras perceive 3D depth in a 2D space. While affine transformations always preserve parallelism , projective transformations allow parallel lines to converge, creating the illusion of perspective.
